YouTube](http://img.shields.io/badge/youtube-nf--core-FF0000?labelColor=000000&logo=youtube)](https://www.youtube.com/c/nf-core) ## Introduction **nf-core/contaminationqc** is a bioinformatics pipeline that checks aligned human sequencing data (BAM/CRAM, e.g. targeted panels such as TSO500) for **sample contamination**, identifies **which sample in the cohort the contaminating DNA came from**, verifies **sample identity** (swaps, longitudinal same-patient samples), compares **inferred with annotated sex** and optionally screens for **non-human contamination** with Kraken2. It scales to thousands of samples per run. 1. Prepare references: FASTA index ([`SAMtools`](https://www.htslib.org/)), restrict somalier sites to panel targets (optional) 2. Extract allele counts at informative sites per sample ([`somalier extract`](https://github.com/brentp/somalier)) 3. Relatedness, CNV-robust concordance and CHARR contamination per batch ([`somalier relate`](https://github.com/brentp/somalier)) 4. Sample identity: hom-hom discordance and genotype (= individual) groups across all samples and batches (`somalier_contam.py identity`) 5. Anchored contamination MLEs between samples of the same individual ([`somalier contamination`](https://github.com/brentp/somalier)) 6. Contamination **source attribution**: mixture model "candidate sample is the contaminant" vs "an unknown person is the contaminant", sharded over receivers (`somalier_contam.py attribute`) 7. Sex check: chrY reads per million autosomal reads ([`SAMtools coverage`](https://www.htslib.org/), MAPQ-filtered) and X heterozygosity (somalier) vs. the samplesheet column `sex` 8. Per-sample calls (`clean`, `source_identified`, `source_ambiguous`, `contaminated_source_not_in_cohort`), sex check, longitudinal and relatedness flags (`somalier_contam.py report`) 9. Optional: non-human screening of unmapped read pairs ([`SAMtools fastq`](https://www.htslib.org/), [`Kraken2`](https://ccb.jhu.edu/software/kraken2/), [`Bracken`](https://ccb.jhu.edu/software/bracken/)) 10. Present QC ([`MultiQC`](http://multiqc.info/))

## Usage > [!NOTE] > If you are new to Nextflow and nf-core, please refer to [this page](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/environment_setup/overview) on how to set-up Nextflow. Make sure to [test your setup](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/run-your-first-pipeline) with `-profile test` before running the workflow on actual data. First, prepare a samplesheet with your input data that looks as follows: `samplesheet.csv`: ```csv sample,bam,bai,individual,batch,sex PATIENT1_TUMOR,/data/PATIENT1_TUMOR.bam,/data/PATIENT1_TUMOR.bam.bai,PATIENT1,RUN01,female PATIENT1_NORMAL,/data/PATIENT1_NORMAL.bam,/data/PATIENT1_NORMAL.bam.bai,PATIENT1,RUN01,female PATIENT2_TUMOR,/data/PATIENT2_TUMOR.cram,/data/PATIENT2_TUMOR.cram.crai,PATIENT2,RUN02,male ``` Each row is one BAM/CRAM. `individual` (optional) groups samples of the same patient: they are checked for identity and used as clean anchors. `batch` (optional, e.g. the sequencing run or library-prep plate) limits the search for contamination sources to samples processed together, which keeps the all-vs-all comparison tractable for thousands of samples. Identity checks always run across all batches. `sex` (optional, `male`/`female`) is compared with the sex inferred from the data. Now, you can run the pipeline using: ```bash nextflow run nf-core/contaminationqc \ -profile \ --input samplesheet.csv \ --fasta /refs/hg19.fa \ --sites /refs/somalier/sites.hg19.vcf.gz \ --panel_bed /refs/tso500_v2_targets.bed \ --outdir ``` ### Screening runs with predefined sites and a Kraken2 database For routine screening (e.g. a nightly run over all samples of the day), keep the reference resources fixed in a parameter file and only change the samplesheet and output directory: `screening.yaml`: ```yaml fasta: /refs/hg19/genome.fa fasta_fai: /refs/hg19/genome.fa.fai sites: /refs/somalier/sites.hg19.vcf.gz # predefined somalier sites with INFO/AF, same build + contig names as the BAMs panel_bed: /refs/tso500_v2_targets.bed # optional: restrict sites to the panel run_kraken2: true kraken2_db: /refs/kraken2/k2_pluspf_16gb # directory or .tar.gz of a prebuilt Kraken2 database kraken2_memory_mapping: true # database on shared storage is memory-mapped instead of loaded per task kraken2_reads: unmapped # classify read pairs with both mates unmapped run_bracken: true # optional, needs a Bracken-enabled database (all prebuilt k2 databases are) somalier_background: /screening/background.csv # optional: .somalier files of earlier runs as extra candidate sources report_top_candidates: 25 # keep the 25 best candidate sources per sample in attribution.pairs.tsv.gz relatedness_flag_threshold: 0.35 # fewer noise-level relatedness flags on small panels with many samples ``` ```bash nextflow run nf-core/contaminationqc \ -profile \ -params-file screening.yaml \ --input samplesheet_2026-11-17.csv \ --outdir /screening/2026-11-17 ``` - **Sites:** use a somalier sites VCF for your genome build that has `INFO/AF` (the contamination models need population allele frequencies), e.g. the sites files from the [somalier releases](https://github.com/brentp/somalier/releases) or a panel-specific set made with `somalier find-sites`. Check with `zgrep -v '^#' sites.vcf.gz | head -1 | grep AF=`. Contig names must match the BAMs and FASTA (`chr1` vs `1`); the pipeline checks this at start-up. - **Kraken2 database:** any Kraken2 database works; prebuilt ones (Standard, PlusPF, capped 8/16 GB versions) are available from the [Kraken2 index zone](https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2). Extract the archive once and point `--kraken2_db` at the directory so it is not unpacked for every run. With thousands of samples, a capped database plus `--kraken2_memory_mapping` keeps memory per task low. - **Background:** the `somalier/extract/*.somalier` files of earlier runs can be listed in a background CSV (`sample,somalier,individual`) so that a contaminant processed on a different day can still be identified. They must have been extracted with the same (panel-restricted) sites. > [!WARNING] > Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI or Nextflow `-params-file` option. Custom config files including those provided by the `-c` Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration _**except for parameters**_; see [docs](https://nf-co.re/docs/running/run-pipelines#using-parameter-files). For more details and further functionality, please refer to the [usage documentation](https://nf-co.re/contaminationqc/usage) and the [parameter documentation](https://nf-co.re/contaminationqc/parameters). ## Pipeline output The main result is `contamination/contaminationqc.summary.samples.tsv` with one row per sample: contamination estimates (CHARR, mixture model), the most likely source sample with its contamination fraction and log-likelihood ratio, a call, and the inferred vs. annotated sex (`sex_check`). To see the results of an example test run with a full size dataset refer to the [results](https://nf-co.re/contaminationqc/results) tab on the nf-core website pipeline page. For more details about the output files and reports, please refer to the [output documentation](https://nf-co.re/contaminationqc/output). ## Credits nf-core/contaminationqc was originally written by Alexander Peltzer. We thank the following people for their extensive assistance in the development of this pipeline: ## Contributions and Support If you would like to contribute to this pipeline, please see the [contributing guidelines](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). For further information or help, don't hesitate to get in touch on the [Slack `#contaminationqc` channel](https://nfcore.slack.com/channels/contaminationqc) (you can join with [this invite](https://nf-co.re/join/slack)). ## Citations An extensive list of references for the tools used by the pipeline can be found in the [`CITATIONS.md`](CITATIONS.md) file.
